R1.matched_blank: the same world with H(0) = 0, everything else equal (§9.12, reading 3): one per machine option serves every p, since at H = 0 the release moves nothing and books nothing, whatever p and the machine (the blanks at the four p and both options are bit-identical on the operator's NumPy kernel). R1.survivors: each fate row minus the matched blank's, at the compared times: the released molecules still present (§9.10, §9.12 reading 4), judged as an amount

cohort.membership: the molecules that detach from their template during [0, 3600 s) (erratum F, §9.19): marked on transcription's own label schedule (a label source's, D296), read at the start of each step (§9.12 reading 7); a molecule re-synthesised from monomers takes the species' label in force and is not a member
cohort.route_1: R1L at p = 0.75, with each machine option: each fate row's share in the window's label times the row, n_F s_window(ts), engine_run's label_<row>_cohort, with the shares of D289 (FR-42's option A; erratum C), the window on transcription's own label schedule and the species' label the base throughout (erratum F): the loss is computed once on the physical row and split by its shares, so the cohort needs no blank and has no departure (erratum B). Judged as an amount, p = 2
cohort.route_2: the host-side check: validation/gene_regulation/cohort.py's known-rate form on the unlabelled run's own releases, int_Q_<release>_<fate>, at its outputs every 60 s, each carried by its fate's declared first-order k, the gross one-way loss (erratum F, §9.19), not the booked net int_D_F, at p = 0.75, with each machine option. It must agree with route 1 within its grid error (§9.8), and it is judged against the references with the tolerance below. At the sheet's own state e^(y_f) is about 9.4e-9, so the gross and net readings agree to about 4e-9

tolerance.estimate: per readout and run, from the engine's three runs at steps 4h, 2h and h: est = max over the compared times of |y(2h) - y(h)| / (2^p - 1), with p as declared
tolerance.tolerance: max(F est, floor_of_scale x scale), with scale = max over the compared times of |y(h)|
tolerance.zero_scale: where scale is 0 (an idle route's counter or heat, as int_Q_tx in R1 or the zero-rate fate at p = 0 or 1), the readout passes only where the reference is 0 at every compared time
tolerance.at_the_floor: where the tolerance is the floor, the readout is judged against the floor and its order check is skipped
tolerance.order_check: elsewhere, the observed order q = log2(max|y(4h) - y(2h)| / max|y(2h) - y(h)|) lies in order_window, else the run is inconclusive
tolerance.cohort_route_2: max(F g, floor_of_scale x scale), with g cohort.known_rate_error on the judged run's outputs (the known-rate form on every output against every second output): the host-side route's own error (§9.8, as erratum F amends it), not a step error, so no order check
tolerance.judged: at step h: a readout passes where max over the compared times of |y(h) - reference| <= its tolerance
tolerance.reported_not_judged: per readout, its observed order q and its effective factor, F (2^q - 1)/(2^p - 1)

factor_source: Roache PJ (1994) Perspective: a method for uniform reporting of grid refinement studies. J. Fluids Eng. 116:405-413: the grid-convergence index GCI = Fs |e|/(r^p - 1), with factor of safety Fs = 3 for two grids at an assumed order and 1.25 for three or more grids at an observed order. Checked against secondary sources (NASA NPARC's grid-convergence tutorial; Phillips and Roy 2014, J. Fluids Eng.); the 1994 paper itself was not reached
floor_reason: FR-25's floor; the lead confirms from the references' README, before the tag, that their resolution lies below it (the builder has not read it)
